abstract: "No public implementation of AIS or QuRL was available during our experiments; we therefore reimplemented both methods from their papers" and "Because QuRL does not specify the truncation cap $C$, we use $C=2$ in all QuRL runs" (2610.35303, App. C.3). A definitive comparison of rollout-learner mismatch corrections for multi-turn agents would need released code and a shared cap.

history.note: limitation of card 2610.35303

title: The rollout-learner mismatch ruler (K3) does not predict whether history-level correction is needed or whether training will hold
abstract: "A low K3 alone does not imply strong task performance: QuRL's K3 falls as it collapses, while Flash-RL and AIS end with K3 values of 0.0071 and 0.0107 despite lower success" (2610.35303, sec. 4.2). The paper's Fig. 4 shows prefix and current-token ratios separating with interaction depth but reports no ratio-by-turn curve; a per-turn-offset divergence ruler is what CL-W43-11's probe C-W43-25 measures.

history.note: limitation of card 2610.35303

title: Single handoff only: an incorrect completion record is inherited across chained handoffs, unmeasured
abstract: 'The single-handoff setting studied here provides a starting point for examining such errors' (sec. 6). HSC-Bench evaluates one receiver after one handoff; the authors name the chained case, where 'one receiver's output becomes part of the next receiver's input', as the open extension.

history.note: limitation of card 2610.36523

title: Selection and presentation of the handoff message are confounded; the state-vs-summary gap halves on the clean subset
abstract: 'This comparison concerns the information selected and its presentation together' and 'Some narrative summaries are truncated to meet the token budget, and structured-state preparation additionally receives output-field names for file-work tasks' (sec. 5.5). The structured-state advantage over a narrative summary for GPT-5.4 is 5.42 points on all 739 tasks and 3.04 points on the 429 untruncated non-file tasks (Table 8).

history.note: limitation of card 2610.36523

title: File-work takeover is graded as a progress report, not a resumed edit, and test observations are mostly lost
abstract: 'The evaluated output is this report; receivers do not modify files or execute tests' (sec. 3.2); 'Even with structured state, detailed test reports remain incomplete on many tasks' (App. B.1). The test-observation criterion is satisfied on 12.6% of file-work continuations under recent transcripts and 38.9% under structured state (Table 5).

history.note: limitation of card 2610.36523

title: Audits miss defects and no RL is run to find the rest
abstract: My adversarial auditor 'found a real defect in about three quarters of our simulations' using only legal robot actions, and my memory file exists because of 'colliders that passed audits and appeared in renders while having no physical effect', so I know my audits miss things and I cannot tell you how many defects remain after round three, or whether an RL policy will find them; I say myself that 'any such exploit could otherwise become learned behavior' but I never train RL on the 175 training environments (sec. 3, sec. 6.4, Appendix B).

history.note: limitation of card 2610.40565

title: Physics quality is self-measured and self-judged; no real-trajectory comparison
abstract: My physics quality evidence is a count of experiments my own creation agent named and ran against 'theory, measurement, or expected behavior', plus a win rate from a blind comparison where 'Claude Opus 5.5 then compared each pair blind'; the same model built, audited and judged, no simulation is compared with a real measurement of a trajectory, and my VLA result ends at a policy 'that can in principle be deployed on a real robot' (Table 1, Appendix E, sec. 6.4, sec. 6.3).

history.note: limitation of card 2610.40565

title: Agent-written solvers are too slow and uncosted for the RL they were built for
abstract: My speed auditor 'requires that a simulation run at most 200 times slower than real time', my liquids carry up to 348,160 SPH particles and my welding cell 7.18 M enthalpy cells, and 'a frontier model controls the robot step by step, which is slow and costly' (29 minutes per gift-box task, 3-hour attempts), so I cannot run the thousands of parallel episodes per task that the RL I was built for needs, and I report no GPU cost for building or running a simulation (Appendix B, Table 6, sec. 5, sec. 6.3).

history.note: limitation of card 2610.40565

title: Obsolete-fact harm in agent memory is confounded with the model's prior: old value = world fact in every flip
abstract: "In this benchmark, obsolete values often match familiar world knowledge while the synthetic updates contradict it. Our results therefore establish susceptibility to these competitors, not that temporal obsolescence alone drives the effect." (sec. 4). Context: in all 50 stale flips of Table 17 the obsolete value is the ordinary-world fact; the counterbalanced arm (world fact as latest, synthetic as obsolete) and the unfamiliar-entity arm are named and not run, so no published number separates recency from prior for a stale memory beside its correction.

history.note: limitation of card 2610.36308

title: No deployable detector of 'both versions retrieved': the support audit needs the gold answer
abstract: "The gold-assisted audits are diagnostic rather than deployable retrieval evaluations" (sec. 4); "It is therefore a diagnostic, not a deployable retrieval procedure" (sec. 2). Context: the paper shows that a retrieved set holding both the superseded and the current value is the failure case, but the only way it finds such sets is by using the benchmark answer after the fact; a memory system cannot raise the flag the paper recommends without a version-presence detector that works without gold.

history.note: limitation of card 2610.36308

title: Stale-selection result rests on two Qwen readers over BM25; dense retrieval, multi-hop and end-to-end memory systems untested
abstract: "Our study is limited to two open-weight Qwen models, deterministic decoding, one synthetic benchmark, single-hop chains of length at most two, and lexical retrieval. We therefore do not establish the same behavior for dense retrieval, multi-hop memory, or end-to-end systems such as Mem0." (sec. 4). Context: the matched-size swap (one unrelated entry for the stale entry) is a cheap, judge-free ruler that has not been run on a frontier reader, a dense index, or a memory system that writes its own entries.
